Hi Sara —

Thanks again for taking the deep dive last week. Attached is a lightweight proposal for the Dedicated uplift we discussed (CT_capacity_proposal_v1.pdf). High-level summary:

- Core reserved slab: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (baseline for 99% of requests)
- Shoulder reserve: additional 4 GPUs for predictable periodic uplift windows (scheduled batch jobs)
- Ephemeral burst pool (preemptible): up to 10 GPUs for short spikes; evicts after 3 minutes of inactivity
- Autoscale triggers: token-rate + queue-latency hybrid policy (see Drive link in metadata)
- Credit model: bursts beyond shoulder are credited back to CT at a 50% rebate applied monthly (to be finalized in SOW)

Questions for you:
1) Does the burst cap of 10 GPUs align with peak experiments you expect in Q4?
2) Any procurement constraints we should know about for credits/commit amendments?

Diego / Priya —

Quick sketch for the customer:

Pricing / crediting (example amortization):
- Baseline Reserved Fee: monthly fixed for 8 GPUs = $48,000/mo (example)
- Shoulder Reserve Fee: monthly fixed for 4 GPUs = $18,000/mo
- Burst Pool (preemptible): charged at on-demand per-minute token rate; when monthly burst minutes exceed the included cushion (10,000 burst-minutes), we convert excess minutes to a dollar credit using an amortization table:
  - Convert excess burst-minutes -> equivalent GPU-minutes -> multiply by on-demand GPU-minute rate ($0.78/GPU-min in this example) -> apply 60% amortized credit spread (i.e., customer receives 60% of overage as credit against next invoice)
- Example: if Catalyze uses 12,000 excess burst-minutes in a month: 2,000 * $0.78 = $1,560 -> credit = $936 applied next invoice.

Operationally (preemptible fallback guidance):
- Eviction model: preemptible instances are best-effort, with 30s notice for graceful checkpointing where possible. Long-running experiments should use periodic checkpointing (recommended cadence: 60–120s) and job-level retries configured to requeue on preemption.
- Best practices: route heavy sweep workloads to a hybrid job runner that prefers shoulder reserve first, then ephemeral pool; enable KV-cache backfill for stateless generation jobs to avoid full cold starts after eviction.
- Autoscale policy: token-rate threshold = 120k tokens/min -> scale shoulder by +2 GPUs per trigger (cooldown 120s); if queue-latency persists > 30s after shoulder scale, ramp ephemeral up to burst cap (10 GPUs) with 30s evaluation windows.

Docs & links: drive doc (capacity model) includes simulation outputs for a 20-GPU spike pattern; I put the trace example from Ethan into the Drive folder for CT.

If Priya okays the ops wording I’ll convert these numbers into a short amendment clause for procurement to review.

1) We’ll keep the preemptible burst cap at 10 GPUs but configure autoscale to prefer shoulder reserve first; simulation on the Drive shows the 20-GPU transient traces you shared can be largely absorbed by shoulder + ephemeral with very small tail drops if jobs follow checkpointing guidance.

2) Credit mechanics: we’ll present the amortized example Ben outlined (dollar credit applied to next invoice). Procurement: we can model three scenarios in the SOW (conservative, expected, aggressive) so you can see the balance of committed fees vs amortized credits.

3) Ops guarantees: we’ll commit to 30s eviction notice for preemptible and recommend checkpoint cadence in the SOW. For business-critical long-running experiments, we recommend scheduling them into reserved window slots (we’ll include a calendar-based shoulder reservation clause).
